Over the past few months, breathing is worse going uphill or up stairs and he gets a pressure-type discomfort in the chest at the same time. Stops, it eases within a few minutes. Never at rest. documents.title: Vascular Surgery Surveillance Letter
documents.author: vascular surgery
documents.body:
VASCULAR SURGERY ASSOCIATES

Dear Doctor,

Mr. Haskins had his aortic surveillance ultrasound on 06/06/2023. His infrarenal aneurysm measures 4.4 cm, compared with 4.3 cm in July 2021. This remains below the threshold for repair. He is asymptomatic from the aneurysm standpoint.

We will repeat the ultrasound in 12 to 24 months. Continued smoking remains the main risk for growth, and we discussed it again.

Sincerely,
Vascular Surgery

documents.title: Cardiology Consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
CARDIOLOGY CONSULTATION
Visit date: 07/19/2023

Reason: progressive exertional dyspnea and chest discomfort.

HPI: 69-year-old man with coronary disease after MI with PCI in 2019, COPD, PAD, infrarenal AAA and a childhood history of rheumatic fever. He reports progressive dyspnea and chest discomfort when walking uphill or climbing stairs, occasional palpitations and mild fatigue. He denies orthopnea, PND and leg swelling.

Medications: lisinopril 20, hydrochlorothiazide 25, metoprolol succinate 50, atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81, olodaterol.
Social: current smoker, about 25 pack-years by his estimate today; drinks socially.

Exam: BP 168/96, pulse 78, BMI 29. Apical impulse sustained and laterally displaced. S1 and S2 normal; no murmurs or gallops. Lungs clear.

ECG: sinus rhythm; LVH by voltage, tall R waves over V5 and V6, and inverted T waves laterally.
Echocardiogram: thickened LV wall, normal ejection fraction, no regional wall motion abnormalities.

Impression: Hypertensive heart disease with LV wall thickening on echo and LVH by ECG voltage criteria. Preserved systolic function, no wall motion abnormality. History of rheumatic fever without valvular disease on today's study.

Plan: Continue current medications. Follow-up with primary care; return here as needed.

AWV subsequent.

Cardiology letter 7/19 reviewed: echo with thickened LV wall, normal EF, no WMA; ECG LVH voltage with lateral T inversions. Their dx: hypertensive heart disease. Plan was continue current meds. Added to problem list.
Vascular surgery 6/6: AAA 4.4 cm, below repair threshold, rescan 12-24 mo.
Still gets the chest discomfort and breathlessness on stairs and hills, unchanged since May. Nothing at rest.

HRA: independent, no falls, no hearing or vision change. PHQ-2 1.
Tobacco 1 ppd, ~48 pk-yr. Alcohol 1-2/wk.

Vitals: BP 163/87, HR 70, SpO2 93%, wt 93.3.
Exam: Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs diminished, prolonged exp. Abd soft, pulsatile mass. No edema. Pedal pulses diminished.

Prevention: LDCT ordered. New FIT kit. RSV vaccine - recommended at his age with COPD and heart disease; will give with flu/COVID in October. Shingrix complete. PCV20 done.

A/P
1. Hypertensive heart disease / HTN - 163/87. Continue lisinopril, HCTZ, metoprolol.
2. CAD s/p MI - stable exertional symptoms after cardiology eval. Continue ASA, statin.
3. COPD - continue olodaterol. Pulm f/u due next summer.
4. AAA 4.4 cm - vascular surgery surveillance.
5. PAD - stable.
6. Tobacco - counseled. Declines.
BMP, CBC, lipids today.

RTC 3-4 mo.
